title: Polynomial-time query outside DynFO
formal: Editorial uniform-initialization variant: is there an isomorphism-invariant polynomial-time Boolean query on some fixed finite relational vocabulary that is not maintainable by any first-order dynamic program with built-in order, addition and multiplication and first-order initialization from the empty input?
definitions:
For each n≥1 the domain is {0,…,n−1}. The fixed input vocabulary contains finitely many relation symbols of fixed arities; initially each input relation is empty. One update inserts or deletes a single tuple in one relation. Redundant insertion and deletion are allowed. A Boolean query assigns a truth value to every finite nonempty input structure and is unchanged by renaming domain elements. Polynomial time means a uniform deterministic Turing algorithm on explicit relation-table encodings.

A dynamic program has a finite auxiliary relational vocabulary, with any fixed finite arities and a designated zero-ary answer relation. The built-ins are order < and ternary Add and Mult, where Add(a,b,c) means a+b=c<n and Mult(a,b,c) means ab=c<n, using ordinary nonmodular arithmetic. For every input relation and update kind, one first-order formula for each auxiliary symbol defines its new tuples from the old state and the changed tuple. Evaluation is simultaneous; quantifiers range over the unchanged finite domain. There are no auxiliary functions.

Initial auxiliary relations are defined by fixed first-order formulas using only equality and the built-ins. The formulas are uniform in n and histories. The answer must be correct initially and after every update prefix. The question asks for one query outside this class, not a family requiring progressively larger arity. This precisely selects FO initialization; it does not ask for separation against arbitrary noncomputable advice in the initial state.
answer_criterion: Provide a concrete polynomial-time query with a complete Lean-checked proof that no program in this model maintains it, or prove every polynomial-time query has such a program. A lower bound only against bounded auxiliary arity or quantifier-free updates is insufficient.
context: The 2017 discussion identifies the absence of general DynFO lower bounds beyond static polynomial-time constraints. The card fixes initialization and arithmetic so the class being separated is unambiguous.
why: An unconditional separation would establish a basic expressive limit of dynamic descriptive complexity.

import_provenance.original_statement: Exhibit a polynomial-time computable Boolean query on finite relational structures that cannot be maintained by first-order update formulas under single-tuple insertions and deletions, even with arbitrary fixed-arity auxiliary relations. This is the central lower-bound frontier emphasized by Schwentick, using the standard empty-input initialization and allowing built-in arithmetic.

sentences: The target is a polynomial-time query that first-order dynamic programs cannot maintain.
Updates change one input tuple and may inspect fixed arithmetic relations.
Auxiliary relations may have arbitrary fixed finite arities.
Initialization is uniformly first-order definable on the empty input.
That initialization choice is explicitly part of the selected variant.
